public_rationale: Zitron offers this as a loose picture of how AI money moves. He says it is 'suggesting' the boom is 'more like' a loop among hyperscalers, NVIDIA and Broadcom, and the two labs. He gives no share, amount, or period. Disclosed investments and compute deals could show that some money moves this way, and other money could show that some does not. Neither would settle whether the boom is 'more like' this loop without a standard he did not give. Turning the analogy into a test of completed recurring flows in a chosen quarter would grade a claim he did not make. So it is not graded.
limitations: A stricter reading that tested specific flows (hyperscaler investment in the labs, lab compute spending with those hyperscalers) could be checked. That reading would add commitments the speaker did not make.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: What is happening suggests the AI boom is more like five or six hyperscalers feeding money to NVIDIA and Broadcom so they can feed money to Anthropic and OpenAI, who then feed that money back to them whenever capacity comes online.

statement.excerpt: And that’s absolutely what’s happening, suggesting that the “AI boom” is more like five or six large companies (hyperscalers) feeding money to two companies (NVIDIA and Broadcom) so that they can feed money to two companies (Anthropic and OpenAI) who then feed that money back to them whenever capacity comes online.

from_speaker: "suggesting that the 'AI boom' is more like"
"five or six large companies (hyperscalers) feeding money to two companies (NVIDIA and Broadcom)"
"so that they can feed money to two companies (Anthropic and OpenAI)"
"who then feed that money back to them whenever capacity comes online"
our_interpretation: The sentence is a hedged analogy ("suggesting", "more like") about the shape of the AI money flow. It is not a claim about a set dollar amount, share, or period.

The emphatic "that's absolutely what's happening" refers to the sentence before it, about new capacity going mostly to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Meta. The flow analogy that follows is presented as what that suggests.
"They" in "so that they can feed money" could mean the hyperscalers or NVIDIA and Broadcom. He gives no threshold for how much of the boom has to look like this before the analogy holds.
No ordinary reading turns this into a test that a filing or dataset could pass or fail without supplying a standard he did not give. So it is treated as not checkable.
criteria.support_condition: Not applicable. The statement is a qualified characterization. It has no stated measure that evidence could meet.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not applicable. Partial or diverse money flows would not refute an analogy offered as 'more like'. He named no share or threshold.
